best_for: Anyone who has to resize, convert or watermark hundreds of images at once on Windows, Mac or Linux, free at home or for a small fee at work.
description:
XnConvert is a batch image converter from XnSoft, the company of Pierre-e Gougelet, who also makes the XnView MP image viewer.

You drop in files or whole folders, build a list of actions, and run the batch in one pass. There are more than 80 actions, from resize, crop and rotate to brightness, contrast, blur, sharpen, watermarks, vignettes and metadata edits, and a list can be saved as a preset for next time. It reads over 500 formats, including camera RAW, HEIC, AVIF, PSD and PDF, and writes about 70. It can also watch folders and apply your edits to new or changed images as they arrive.

points.title: Free at home, paid at work
points.text: XnConvert is freeware for private and educational use, non-profit groups included. Using it in a company requires a license, listed at the time of reading at 15 euros for one seat, falling to 6.50 euros a seat for 100 or more.

points.title: Closed source, no ads
points.text: XnConvert is proprietary, with all rights reserved by its author, and XnSoft states it carries no adware or spyware. The interface comes in more than 20 languages.

points.title: From batch to command line
points.text: A finished action list can be exported to NConvert, XnSoft's command-line converter, for use in scripts. XnConvert itself also accepts files, or a text file listing them, on its command line.

points.title: Current Windows builds need Windows 10
points.text: The latest version needs 64-bit Windows 10 or 11. XnSoft keeps 1.117 for Windows 7 and 8, and 1.98.0 is the last 32-bit build. The Windows listing keeps 16 versions, back to 1.95.0 with x86 installers, and every installer sets XnConvert up for all users of the PC.

points.title: Only the newest Mac version here
points.text: The Mac app is one universal build for Intel and Apple silicon. XnSoft points users of macOS 10.13 to 12 to version 1.117, which this listing cannot offer, as it keeps only the current Mac version.

points.title: The Linux Flatpak runs behind
points.text: The Flathub package is verified as XnSoft's own but is x64 only, and at the time of reading it was at 1.116, two releases behind Windows and Mac. XnSoft's own Linux downloads (DEB, TGZ and AppImage) are for Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 11.6, RHEL 8.6 or newer.
